newsitem.title: SWEDEN: No change in public EMU sentiment-Swedish FinMin.
newsitem.headline: No change in public EMU sentiment-Swedish FinMin.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Friday he had not seen a change in Swedes' negative opinion about membership of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
"I have not seen a positive change when it comes to public opinion about EMU," Asbrink told journalists after a meeting with the Swedish parliament's EU commission.
A survey by pollster Skop, published on April 1, showed almost a quarter of respondents gave a flat no to EMU membership, while 55 percent wanted to wait and see or were uncertain.
Only one in every five Swedes wanted the country to be in the first wave to join in 1999.
Asbrink reiterated that his own opinion about EMU membership and the opinion of the minority Social Democratic government would be disclosed before this summer, at least before July.
The government will then await a formal decision by the party congress this autumn.
Asbrink also said that the issue of whether the Swedish constitution had to be changed ahead of possible EMU membership should be solved before the summer.
